clue.text: One describes Scottish island facing decline in recession

indicators.note: one thing facing another sits right up against it, so the two parts are set side by side
something in recession goes backwards, so the joined letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to rot is to decline or decay
Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

explanation.surface: Someone recounts how a Scottish island fell on hard times during an economic slump.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the decline should come first for the reversal to work; read as island and decline face to face, the pair together turns round to give NARRATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrator is the person who tells or recounts a story, so is one who describes events.

clue.text: That's the very same sound!

blocks.note: first meaning: the call in a card game when two matching cards turn up
second meaning: a sudden sharp cracking noise

explanation.walkthrough: The card game is played by calling out when two identical cards appear, which is the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the exclamation shouted on spotting identical cards and a sharp crack like fingers clicking.

clue.text: A girl embraced love with declaration

indicators.note: to embrace something is to hold it in your arms, so one set of letters wraps round another

blocks.note: taken as written
Val is a girl's name
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A girl hugged her sweetheart while declaring her feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a link word but supplies a letter: the girl's name holds both love and with.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is an open statement or admission, a synonym for a declaration.

clue.text: Less inclined to give praise

blocks.note: first meaning: more level, having less of a slope
second meaning: to compliment someone, often insincerely

explanation.walkthrough: 'Less inclined' reads as less willing, but it means less sloping: the comparative of an adjective for level ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the comparative of a level-surface adjective and also a verb for paying lavish compliments.

clue.text: Put it another way — return per share is terrible

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the word is read backwards
something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An investor complains that the dividend per share is dreadful, putting it more bluntly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return per share' looks like a financial term, but 'return' acts on 'per' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To rephrase something is to express it again in different words.

clue.text: Pardon given by a bishop is the answer

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the chess notation for bishop
a solution is the answer to a problem

explanation.surface: A bishop's forgiveness is presented as the remedy for sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is the formal release from sin granted by a priest, a forgiveness or pardon.

clue.text: Good to make a mark outside the church

indicators.note: one thing outside another surrounds it, so these letters go round the rest

blocks.note: a dent is a mark or hollow in a surface
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A well-behaved person leaves graffiti on a church wall, which seems unlikely.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent means respectable or of acceptable quality, both senses of good.

clue.text: One very absorbed by erotic entertainment

indicators.note: something absorbed by another is soaked up inside it, so those letters sit within

blocks.note: carnal means sexual or erotic
I is the Roman numeral for one
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Someone is utterly engrossed in a racy show.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnival is a festival with processions, music and dancing, a large public entertainment.

clue.text: A sign some resemble me?

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so a run of letters is taken from inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a few people look like them, as though spotting a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a symbol or badge representing something, so a kind of sign.

clue.text: Cut in yield

blocks.note: first meaning: to trim short, as with hair
second meaning: the harvest a field produces

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a reduction in output, but the two words are separate meanings joined by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for trimming something short and a noun for a season's harvest.

clue.text: See one drawing tall building

blocks.note: to watch is to see or observe
one who tows, pulling something along behind

explanation.surface: An artist is spotted sketching a skyscraper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests sketching, but here it means pulling, as a horse draws a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchtower is a high structure from which a lookout keeps guard, a tall building.

clue.text: Walk to turn at end of road

indicators.note: placing something at the end of another tacks it on after, so the parts join in sequence

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a road
to roll is to turn over and over

explanation.surface: Directions for a walk: turn when you reach the end of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely walk, so the noun is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Free time when attacks are to be expected

definitions.text: time when attacks are to be expected

blocks.note: open means free of restriction
a season is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone has spare time, but it is a period when they will be ambushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' does double duty: it supplies the second word and also heads the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is literally the legal hunting period, and figuratively a spell when someone is a target of criticism.

clue.text: Leave girl with acute problem

indicators.note: a word with a problem is in trouble, so its letters are disordered

blocks.note: Eva is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl suffering a sharp medical complaint is told to go.
explanation.definitionFit: To evacuate is to leave or withdraw from a place, usually because of danger.

clue.text: Perhaps Virginia is a sycophant

blocks.note: first meaning: a climbing plant, of which the Virginia variety is an example
second meaning: an informal word for a toady

explanation.walkthrough: Virginia looks like a woman's name or a US state, but it is the climbing plant with red autumn leaves; 'Perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a trailing or climbing plant and, in slang, a crawling flatterer.

clue.text: Not all alone, sadly, after opening stretch

indicators.note: not all of a word means part of it is dropped
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short at the front
a gate is an opening in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: Someone, sad and lonely, stretches out after a first night.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first letter of 'alone' leaves LONE to be jumbled; 'after' sits awkwardly, since the gate actually comes after.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate is to make longer, which is what stretching does.

clue.text: Produce vicar took back to food shop

indicators.note: taking something back returns it the way it came, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop
Rev is short for Reverend, a vicar's title

explanation.surface: A vicar returns some farm produce to the delicatessen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' reads as a noun for vegetables, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver results or goods is to produce them, as in delivering on a promise.

clue.text: Premature to grab flourished unfinished drink?

indicators.note: to grab something is to take hold of it, so one word closes round the other
something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: early means before the expected time
grew means thrived or flourished

explanation.surface: Someone too hasty snatches a half-finished drink that was going well.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Grey is a black tea flavoured with bergamot, a popular hot drink.

clue.text: Delivers one's belongings

blocks.note: first meaning: brings about, as in effecting a change
second meaning: personal property

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a courier dropping off someone's things; the verb sense is to bring about.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means achieves or accomplishes; as a plural noun it means personal possessions.

clue.text: First-born to hurry away after rejection

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word it is attached to

blocks.note: the initial of the word
to rush off is to leave in a hurry

explanation.surface: An eldest child storms off after being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First-born' looks like one unit meaning an eldest child; split it, and 'First' takes the first letter of 'born'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brush-off is a curt dismissal or snub, so a rejection.

clue.text: Somewhat unrestrained with her art

indicators.note: unrestrained means let loose, so the letters run free into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Her artwork is described as fairly uninhibited.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather, as an adverb, means to some degree or fairly, the same as somewhat.

clue.text: Criticise attempt to find a little room

blocks.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A critic slates someone's effort at locating a bit of space.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry is a small storeroom for food, a little room off a kitchen.

clue.text: Mixture left is a delicate shade

blocks.note: a paste is a soft moist mixture
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A painter notes that the paint left over makes a soft colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastel is a pale, soft colour, so a delicate shade or tint.

clue.text: They're behind star turn by royal horseman outside

indicators.note: to turn something is to twist it round, so the letters are rearranged
one thing outside another wraps round it, so these letters surround the next

blocks.note: taken as written
split as horse plus man: gee-gee is a childish word for a horse, and Les is a man's name
R stands for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A star act is upstaged by a mounted royal guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star turn' reads as a headline act and 'royal horseman' as a guardsman; split them as star / turn and royal / horse / man.
explanation.definitionFit: Stragglers are those who lag behind the rest of a group.

clue.text: About time it's barred

blocks.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone declares it is high time something was banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barred' suggests forbidden, but the definition describes something fitted with bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A cage is an enclosure built of metal bars, so it is literally barred.

clue.text: Shellfish student found in river

indicators.note: in places one item within another, so the letter sits inside the river

blocks.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A student comes across a shellfish while wading in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A clam is a bivalve mollusc, a kind of shellfish.

clue.text: Engineers arrange holiday location

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
to sort is to arrange

explanation.surface: Army engineers organise a place for a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort is a place people go for holidays, such as a seaside town.

clue.text: Ordered green tea for young person

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so these letters are re-sequenced

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone requested green tea on behalf of a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is someone aged thirteen to nineteen, a young person.
